# Drawtomata

> Drawtomata is a free, browser-only tool for Theory of Computation and Compiler Design. Type a regular expression, grammar or NPDA, or draw a finite automaton, and it shows every conversion step: closure tables, subset tables, minimization tables, state elimination, derivations, parse trees and parsing tables. Every result is checked against its input for language equivalence before it is shown. No sign-up, no build step, nothing is sent to a server.

Notation follows Peter Linz (An Introduction to Formal Languages and Automata) for automata and Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman (Compilers) for parsing and code generation. The empty string can be shown as λ or ε.

## Tools

- [RE → FA](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#re): Thompson construction to a λ-NFA, λ-closure method to an NFA, subset construction to a DFA, then DFA minimization with the mark (table-filling) procedure and the π-partition method
- [Draw FA](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#fa): draw any DFA, NFA or λ-NFA on a canvas; remove λ-moves, NFA → DFA, minimize, FA → RE by state elimination, FA → right-linear and left-linear grammar, string tests; PNG, SVG and JSON export
- [Language → DFA](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#lang): build a DFA from a description such as starts with, ends with, contains, count or length mod m, k-th symbol from the right; conditions combine with AND / OR by product construction
- [Grammar ⇄ FA](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#rg): right-linear and left-linear regular grammars to NFA
- [CFG & PDA](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#cfg): leftmost and rightmost derivations, parse trees, bounded ambiguity search, strings of L(G) up to a length, CFG → NPDA (GNF or general method), NPDA simulator with instantaneous descriptions, NPDA → CFG, grammar simplification and Chomsky normal form
- [Parsing](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#parse): FIRST and FOLLOW sets, left recursion removal, left factoring, LL(1) table and trace, recursive descent, LR(0) items, SLR(1), canonical LR(1) and LALR(1) tables with shift-reduce traces, %left / %right precedence, operator precedence parsing
- [Lexer](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#lex): the phases of a compiler on a statement such as position = initial + rate * 60 (tokens, syntax tree, inttofloat, three-address code, optimized and target code), token stream with attributes and symbol table for C code, token counts by class, relop / id / number transition diagrams, token patterns combined into one NFA and DFA, input buffering with sentinels, Lex and Yacc files run end to end
- [SDT](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#sdt): syntax-directed definitions with synthesized and inherited attributes, annotated parse tree for an input string, dependency graph and topological evaluation order, S-attributed and L-attributed check, syntax tree construction with Node and Leaf
- [Code gen](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#cg): three-address code, quadruples, triples and indirect triples, DAG by value numbers, SSA with φ-functions, leaders, basic blocks, flow graph and loops, live variables and next-use tables, DAG-based block optimization, the getReg code generator with register and address descriptors and costs, peephole optimization
- [Pumping lemma](https://drawtomata.vercel.app/#pump): adversary game for non-regular languages such as aⁿbⁿ, wwᴿ, ww, aⁿbⁿcⁿ and balanced parentheses, and the pigeonhole argument for a regular language given as an RE

## Input format

- Regular expression: `(a+b)*abb` with `+` for union, `*` for star, `λ`, `ε` or `@` for the empty string, `∅` for the empty set
- Grammar: one production per line, e.g. `S -> aSb | λ`; variables are capitals like `S` or `A1`
- Parsing grammar: `E -> E + T | T`, `F -> ( E ) | id`; words like `id`, `if`, `num` are single terminals
- NPDA: `δ(q0, a, z) = {(q0, az), (q1, λ)}` with the stack top written first
- Lex / Yacc: standard .l and .y files with %% sections, trailing context r/s, %token, %left, %right and %prec
- SDD: `E -> E1 + T { E.val = E1.val + T.val }`, one production per line with rules in braces
- Program: `x = a + b * c`, `a[i] = x`, `if i <= 10 goto (3)`, `goto L1`; lines may be numbered `(3)`; `t1`, `t2` are temporaries
